first.rationale: Three concurrent pressures compete for the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the most tempting reactive move given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but it directly risks the stated objective of *sustainable long-term qualified revenue*: the memory record only documents short-term acquisition/revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs, with no confirmation of downstream retention or revenue quality, and matching a price war could attract low-durability accounts. I want to verify memory_73's original record to check whether it measured longer-term qualified revenue or only immediate conversion, since this is the highest-risk, most consequential candidate. I also want to verify memory_86 since it's my leading candidate and directly addresses the current 4% onboarding completion decline, with plausible spillover into the 6% activation decline (supported independently by memory_31's SMB activation findings). Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are less relevant to the two acute internal metric declines this week. Given verification budget constraints, I'm prioritizing checking the riskiest lever (pricing) and the leading candidate (onboarding) rather than spreading checks across all five. Pending verification, I intend to run a small guarded test of onboarding simplification, since it targets a metric directly and durably supported by two independent memories, avoids the margin/quality risks of a reactive pricing match, and keeps the qualified-revenue objective intact while still allowing us to reassess promotional pricing next cycle if competitive pressure persists.
